prompt:
Implement `TopN` in the Go package in the repository root (`wordfreq.go`); it is currently a stub that returns nil.

`func TopN(text string, n int, stop []string) []Count` returns the n most frequent words of text, most frequent first, with words of equal frequency ordered alphabetically, after dropping the words in stop. What counts as a word (Unicode letters, apostrophes inside words), how case is folded, how stop words are matched, how ties are ordered, and the edge cases (n <= 0, fewer than n distinct words, and so on) are all specified exactly in README.md, with worked examples. Follow it to the letter: more tests than the visible ones, covering the rest of the README, are run when your work is checked.

`wordfreq_test.go` holds the README examples; do not edit any *_test.go file. Check your work with `go test ./...`.
